conventions.convention: The forward unitary DFT has negative exponential sign and factor N^(-1/2); the inverse has positive sign and the same factor. The engineering DFT is √N times the unitary DFT. Cyclic convolution is unnormalised.

DCT-II uses j,k=0,...,N−1, cosine argument π(j+1/2)k/N, and extension entries E_j=E_(2N−1−j)=x_j. DST-I uses j,k=1,...,N, sine argument πjk/(N+1), endpoint zeros at 0 and N+1, and antisymmetric reflected entries.

Successful operationwise arithmetic uses nearest-even binary rounding and excludes every nonzero subnormal or overflowing exact intermediate. Complex multiplication uses four rounded real products followed by one rounded subtraction and one rounded addition.

Phase certification uses finite directed-rounding formats and budgets, returns the lower-left corner of the cosine/sine rectangle, and bounds its modulus error by an upward-rounded sum of coordinate widths. Exhausted certification may return inconclusive.
The interval evaluator's π=4 arctan(1) is identified with the canonical Fourier π defined from the first positive cosine zero.

Computed FFT inputs and certified phase operands must belong coordinatewise to the same arithmetic representable set. The radix-two routine returns a unitary transform; the arbitrary-length routine returns an approximate unnormalised DFT.

The arbitrary-length exactness and O(N log N) count concern the formal exact-constant model with sufficient subdivision depth. Integer factor search, phase generation, interval evaluation, storage, and bit complexity are excluded.

load_bearing.statement: Whenever alg-na-certified-unit-circle-phase returns certified(ŵ,ε) on rational input q, its output satisfies |ŵ−exp(πiq)|≤ε≤τ.
Let u≤1/16. For z,w∈C, the specified six-operation complex product satisfies |fl_C(zw)−zw|≤3u|z||w| if every nonzero intermediate is normal and no operation overflows.
For u≤1/16, |w|=1 and |ŵ−w|≤ε≤1/4, a successful butterfly with every exact nonzero real intermediate normal has pair error at most (10u+ε) times the Euclidean norm of its input pair.

For N=2^m and a successful execution with u≤1/16 and every twiddle error at most εtw≤1/4, put η=10u+εtw. The forward and conjugated inverse errors are at most ((1+η)^m−1) times the input norm; if mη≤1 this is at most 2mη times that norm.

For successful length-M=2^q convolution with u≤1/16 and twiddle errors bounded by εtw≤1/4, define ρ=(1+10u+εtw)^q−1, εp=3u, εs=2u+u² and λ=2ρ+ρ²+εp(1+ρ)². The cyclic error is at most √M[λ+ρ(1+λ)+εs(1+ρ)(1+λ)]||a||₂||b||₂; the same bound applies to the retained linear-convolution outputs.
For N≥1, M≥2N−1 and the stated padded chirp arrays, (F_N x)(k)=N^(-1/2)γ_k(a*_M b)_k for 0≤k<N, and a*_M b=√M F_M^(-1)((F_M a)⊙(F_M b)).

For integers r,s≥2, N=rs, strided inputs x^(u)_v=x_(u+rv), and y^(k₂)_u=exp(−2πiuk₂/N)(F_s x^(u))(k₂), one has (F_N x)(k₂+sk₁)=(F_r y^(k₂))(k₁) throughout the stated index ranges, without a coprimality assumption.
For positive sequence lengths n,m and M≥n+m−1, zero padding makes the first n+m−1 cyclic-convolution entries equal the full linear convolution and makes every remaining cyclic entry zero.
For the stated DCT-II matrix C, CCᵀ=diag(N,N/2,...,N/2), with the displayed inverse formula; the even extension satisfies (F_(2N) E_N x)(k)=√(2/N)exp(πik/(2N))X_k for 0≤k<N.

concerns.concern: F2 says, “The DCT-II inverse is a_0=X_0/N and a_k=2X_k/N for k≥1,” citing thm-na-dct-ii-orthogonality-inverse-and-dft-extension. That supplier gives reconstruction of sample coordinates by a cosine sum, not this Chebyshev coefficient-recovery rule. The displayed rule is supplied by thm-na-dct-ii-chebyshev-coefficient-extraction, already cited in F1. The numerical example remains correct, but F2 conflates sample inversion with coefficient extraction and attributes the formula to the wrong statement.

Proof 3.1 says, “Applying the inverse in [F3] and dividing by √M ... proves the displayed FFT convolution representation of c.” Applying the inverse to F_M c=√M((F_M a)⊙(F_M b)) already yields the claimed c=√M F_M^(-1)((F_M a)⊙(F_M b)); the stated additional division instead gives a formula for c/√M. The displayed conclusion is correct, but the description of the scaling operation is inaccurate.

seams_checked.note: The actual supplier is the operationwise binary nearest-even model. Complex products use its six operations; roots and real scalings are rounded as specified. The error claims retain successful zero-or-normal intermediate hypotheses and do not import a factorization stability result.

The phase routine supplies directed angle enclosures to finite cosine/sine DAG evaluations, uses only finite range-containing outputs, and preserves inconclusive/overflow branches. The separate π bridge uses the supplier's exact Machin identity with its integral-defined arctangent.

alg-box-muller-finite-bit-transform passes rational q=2u₂ and fixed admissible phase controls, imports the certified absolute phase-error bound, and propagates failed certification. Its page explicitly requires uniform certification over all bit inputs for the distribution-error theorem.

alg-na-computed-clenshaw-curtis-via-fast-dft passes representable samples, length 2n and all declared controls to the unnormalised arbitrary-length DFT. Its endpoint/interior DCT-I rescalings match that convention. It propagates supplier failures and makes no new end-to-end stability claim.
